bib.title: Natural Language Basics (Chapter 1, Text Analytics with Python)

question: What concepts of natural language, linguistics, syntax, semantics, corpora, NLP and text analytics does a text analytics practitioner need before the techniques in later chapters?
contributions: Introduces natural language, philosophy of language, language acquisition and speech acts
Covers English syntax (words, phrases, clauses), dependency vs constituency grammars, word order typology
Covers lexical semantic relations, semantic networks, propositional and first order logic
Lists popular text corpora and shows NLTK access to Brown, Reuters and WordNet
Defines NLP applications and text analytics

limits: Conceptual survey; no experiments, no preprocessing, bag of words, TF-IDF or embeddings content (those are deferred to Ch 3 and later).
Code uses Python 2.7 and the NLTK API of 2016; print statements and u'' strings no longer run on Python 3.
Spacy-era dependency labels (prep, pobj) from a 2016 parser; the chapter says trees vary by parser and training data.
Calls a dependency tree a DAG and says dependency grammars have a one-to-one word correspondence; Figure 1-8 labels vary by parser.
Tomlin 1986 survey figures are not re-derived; the adverb phrase example is mislabeled 'adjective phrase' in the text (pretty soon).
NLP application descriptions (speech recognition 'most difficult', Siri/Cortana) are dated.
practices: Know the constituents hierarchy word < phrase < clause < sentence because it underpins text processing, annotation and parsing (p10).
Annotate text with POS tags, stems, lemmas, dependency and constituency structure to make corpora useful for NLP (p38).
Convert each document to a vector of word weights (frequency, occurrence or other) before applying learning algorithms (p50).
Clean and process text to remove noisy terms (text pre-processing) before modelling (p50).
Use universal quantifiers with implication and existential quantifiers with conjunction in FOL; the reverse gives wrong semantics (p35).
Install all NLTK resources with nltk.download('all') or select components with the GUI (p41).

terms.definition: one developed and evolved by humans through natural use and communication, rather than constructed and created artificially, like a computer programming language
also known as text mining, the methodology and process followed to derive quality and actionable information and insights from textual data
the canonical or base form for a set of words (a lexeme); wordforms are inflected forms of the lemma
a part of the word to which various affixes can be attached
word-based grammar of labeled, asymmetrical word-word links; the word with no dependency is the root, usually the verb; word order is not depicted
phrase structure grammar representing a sentence as hierarchically ordered constituents via phrase structure rules such as S -> NP VP; order is preserved
technique for finding out the constituents in a sentence, including POS tags and phrases
a large and structured collection of texts or textual data, written or spoken, often electronic
specialized corpus annotated with dependency or constituency parse trees, used to build POS taggers and parsers
WordNet entity grouping lexical units by semantic similarity, e.g. synonyms

terms.term: homonym / homograph / homophone / heteronym / heterograph / polyseme / capitonym
terms.definition: word-relation types distinguished by shared spelling, pronunciation and relatedness of meaning (bat; lead; pair/pear; tear; to/too/two; bank; march/March)
hyponym is a subclass word with specific sense; hypernym is the more generic superclass word (fruit vs mango)
PL treats propositions as atomic with truth values and five operators; FOL adds objects, relations, functions, quantifiers and variables
open classes (N, V, ADJ, ADV) accept new words; closed classes such as pronouns do not
locutionary (delivery), illocutionary (significance; Searle's five classes: assertives, directives, commissives, expressives, declarations), perlocutionary (effect on receiver)
cleaning and processing text to remove noisy terms before converting a document to a vector of word weights
